Inherited from Old East Slavic сорокъ (sorokŭ, “a bunch of 40 sable pelts; forty”), displaced четꙑре десѧте (četyre desęte, “forty”) (< Proto-Slavic *četyre desęte (“forty”)). Further etymology is unclear. In the past regarded as borrowed from Medieval Greek σαράκοντα (sarákonta, “40”), but this etymology is dubious for phonetic and semantic reasons. The older meaning is a bunch of sable pelts. May be related to соро́чка (soróčka); compare Old Norse serkr (“shirt; 200 furs”), archaic Slovak meru (“40”) from Hungarian mérő (“sack”).
